- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and model overestimates, reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days to avoid overshoot.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and model overestimates, apply downward bias of 3–7% to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75.0), reduce forecast by 1–3% per day for 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a 1–3% downward adjustment to the 30-day average.
- When sentiment is high but price drops sharply, model tends to overreact — apply a 2–4% downward correction to prevent lagged overcorrection.
- If sentiment is low and price is stable, model often overpredicts — apply a 1–3% downward bias to avoid false optimism.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70.0, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect mean reversion toward lower range.
- If sentiment is high and forecast is low, model may be underestimating — increase by 1–3% to avoid missing bullish momentum.
